title: Minimum Operations to Make Array Equal to Target
summary: Given two equal-length arrays nums and target, each containing positive integers, determine the least number of operations needed to transform nums into target.
statement: Given two equal-length arrays nums and target, each containing positive integers, determine the least number of operations needed to transform nums into target. An operation consists of selecting any subarray of nums and either increasing or decreasing each element by one.
constraints: nums and target are nonempty equal-length positive-integer arrays.
One operation selects a contiguous subarray and adds one to every element, or subtracts one from every element.
Return the minimum operations needed to transform nums into target.
hints: View each required signed difference as stacked positive or negative unit layers across indices.
Same-sign neighboring stacks reuse their overlapping layers; a sign change must start all layers anew.
Start abs(d[0]); add max(0,abs(cur)-abs(prev)) for same sign, else abs(cur).
Each counted layer start requires one subarray operation, and extending every layer until it ends constructs a matching optimal sequence.
editorial: Each counted layer start requires one subarray operation, and extending every layer until it ends constructs a matching optimal sequence.

tests.explanation: Increase the whole array once, then increase only the last element once, totaling two.
Required differences change sign, so positive and negative adjustment layers cannot share operations.
